items.note: Both plans carry B1 (rows 0-1 remove, 2-5 add, 6-7 restore; net change (JV+RG)x independent of a,c), B2 (|S cap T| mod 2, side wires cancel intersection one, self coefficient one), B3 ((|S cap T|-1)/2, side cancels zero and two) and B4 (stages (x,y)->(x,y+x)->(-y,y+x)->(-y,x) with restored auxiliaries): A K1.a.1-K1.a.3, K1.b; B S5.1.1-S5.1.4, S5.2. Neither gives the neighbour or wire counts (lines 767-782).

Both state the invariant (stored array = D_v applied to the logical array), commutation of a common frame with a pointwise linear gate, the operator D_out S D_in^{-1}, and the signed-route formula eps_w D_sink(rho(w)) D_source(w)^{-1} including auxiliary roles (A K2, K2.a-c; B S5.3, S5.3.1-3; paper 804-825).

differences.what: The label construction itself: triple indicator vectors with <t_S,t_T>=|S cap T|-1 over Q (form I-J/9) and the dot product over F_2, so triple lines are nondegenerate and neighbouring triple lines orthogonal. A never says what the labels are.

Side-wire nesting: t_X orthogonal to t_Y gives <t_X> contained in t_Y-perp, which is what makes the side edge 2->5 increasing. B omits the h-2 dimension of the complement <t_X,t_Y>-perp; A has nothing.

items.note: Both carry L3 (sources N, sinks Wm-N, signed Wm-2N, only decrease centre 3->4 losing h, L=Ich, absolute Wm-2N+2L) and L5 (100/539, 101/539). Neither gives the residual table (L1) or the F_2 orthonormal-basis argument (L4). B adds the indicator-vector construction and L2, which A lacks.

Both give rank(P_V-P_U)=dim V-dim U, the N exceptional source edges 2P_{U_a} of rank one, s_b=W_b m-N+2L_b with deficit N-2L_b>0, and the endpoint condition M_out(rho(w))-M_in(w)=I_m turning the frames Phi_M into H<-H+D on every role (A K3.B.1-4, KS.frame; B S5.4.7.1-3, S5.9.3; paper 1115-1171).

differences.what: Weight is additive mod 4 for orthogonal binary vectors, so q_V-q_U = sum over an orthonormal residual basis of wt(v)[v.x].
wt(v) odd, so the phase is i^{eps[v.x]} = (1+i^eps)/2 + (1-i^eps)/2 (-1)^{v.x}; Hadamard conjugation turns it into the translation kernel aI+bX_v or its inverse.

Endpoint repair: the pair X_a->Y_a carries C^{-1} on the 27 coordinates of supp(u_a), turned into C by C=iZC^{-1}Z with sign and phase corrections. A states only a generic 'after the source and sink corrections'.
The count s_c=W_c m-2N+2L_c with deficit 2N-2L_c>0 (no extra source ranks). A never gives s_c's value or shows s_c<W_c m.

items.note: Both say the edge change is one kernel per orthonormal residual vector and that the s_c kernels act on slots of f columns (P3 via A S3.1.d / B S5.11.4). Only B derives why: weight additivity, odd weight and Hadamard conjugation (P1, P2). Only B gives the 27-coordinate endpoint repair (P4) and the formula for s_c.

differences.what: The conclusion for both networks, s_b/W_b<m^tau and s_c/W_c<m^sigma with tau=sigma. A K3.C concludes s/W<m^tau for an unspecified single deficit and never establishes sigma for the complex network.

items.note: Both carry R1 (L/N<1/2, deficit N-2L>0) and R4 (deficit above 20*2^-50, log m<20, so m^{1-2^-50}>m(1-eta)). Only B gives the two exact deficits (R2, R3) and the bound for the complex network that the layer recurrence uses.

Both state the O(V) elementary stream operations and the controlled shift/unit multiplication by fibre splitting and re-merging (A S2.1, S2.2; B S3, S4; paper 491-639). A's 'two pieces merged in opposite order' and B's vaguer 'blocks re-merged in another order' are both faithful.

differences.what: The condition on the modulus: for the fixed finite set of matrices there is a fixed odd prime q. B states only its existence, not that it avoids every denominator so that the factors stay invertible mod q^b, so M2 is only partly present. A says nothing about the choice of q.

items.note: Both state A=E_1 Pi E_2 without the elimination proof (M1 absent in both). Both have M3 (descending-order O(V) triangular updates) and M4 (D_j<-D_j+H_i, interchange, D_j<-H_i-D_j; a interchanges): A K5.a-c, B S5.8.1-4. B's mention of the fixed odd prime is the only difference.

differences.what: Explicit k=0 base case by the single-digit stream operation.
Each role stream's row count is divisible by W^{k-1}, and child fields have b=e/m digits.

items.note: Both carry the row split into W streams of volume V/W, the frame Phi_M with endpoint condition, the three-update swap, exactly s calls, F_0=O(1), F_k<=(s/W)F_{k-1}+O(1) with both cases of the geometric sum, the depth-first parking schedule and descriptor cost (paper 1491-1615). The small differences balance.

differences.what: The choice rho=ceil(k log W/(2 log q)) giving row range R=q^{2 rho}>=W^k (A says only rho=O(log e)).
Removing padding and reversing the joining moves costs O(V log(2e)), absorbed in O(Ve^tau).

items.note: Both carry the high-digit row field, padding to a multiple of W^k, the base-m decomposition, the geometric cost sum and padding binary ranges to [q^e]. B adds the explicit rho choice that guarantees enough rows, and the cleanup cost.

differences.what: The change of basis P_M (M invertible over F_2 whose first columns are the residual basis) puts the directional kernels C_{v_j} onto coordinate slots: C_{U+}C_{U-}^{-1} = P_M (prod C_{e_j}^{eps_j}) P_M^{-1}. This is the step that makes each residual vector one child call on a slot. A has no P_M.

Gaussian elimination writes M as at most m(m-1)+3m elementary row additions, each XORing selected bits of two whole slots. This is the 'fixed number of row additions' that packed-selected-bit-addition performs.

items.note: Both carry the edge kernel product, the inverse-child identity (C^{-1})^{tensor f}=(-i)^f Z C Z, exactly s_c children on f=e/m axes, C^{tensor e} on every role, and H_0^{tensor D}=b^D S_D C^{tensor D} S_D. A omits the P_M conjugation and the reduction to row additions, which is how the kernels become slot calls.

differences.what: Why the packed shift is correct off the bad set: guard values in [10, 2^{K-1}-11] and displacement at most eight keep every segment in range, so no carry or borrow crosses segments.
The full time bound (movement O(V(L^tau+1)), scans O(M A^3+V), radix passes O(|B| A(R+A))) and the family conditions making the extra terms o(1). A writes only 'plus negligible terms'.
Application: a fixed binary change of basis is a fixed number of such row additions, so it and its inverse cost O(V((eK)^tau+1)).
The omitted top selected position j_{f-1} is handled by a separate two-bit XOR.

items.note: Both carry the eight conditional additions and their net map, packed cyclic shifts, the bad-set bound delta_bad=min{1,80(f-1)2^-K}, T_0 S_0^{-1} permuting the bad set, and the sort repair. B adds the no-carry argument, the full cost terms and the change-of-basis application. A adds only the last-position XOR.

differences.what: The exponent condition tau(1+c/beta)<lambda, which makes the internal overhead O(e^{tau(1+c/beta)}+1)=O(e^lambda); A asserts O(e^lambda) without the condition.
The stopping rule beta=1/2, justified by individual C kernels costing O(Ve).

items.note: Both carry the rows from the first q_0 chunks, children of volume V/W, F(e)<=(s/W)F(e/m)+O((eK)^tau+1) with leaves O(e), the geometric internal sum, the leaf bound e^sigma d^{beta(1-sigma)} and the lambda' condition. B also states the exponent condition and the value of beta.

differences.what: The constants C_1=max{20,nu+3} and C_0=128mB^2 that define Delta. A uses Delta=ceil(C_0 d^{C_1}) without defining C_0 or C_1 here.
Concatenating at most md pieces, the individual kernels and the outer diagonals gives the total below 128mB^2 d^{nu+3} <= C_0 d^{C_1}. A stops at A(e)<=8B^2 d^{nu+1}.

The computed chirp transform: phase numerators mod 2r, x_0=Q_p(conj(a~).x), y_0=M~_C(a~,x_0), C~(x)=Q_p(conj(a~).y_0), with exact counterpart QF_t x.
Why there are two occurrences of S: (u*v)/S^2, then w=(u*v)/S, then 2^{2b+4}S w is the integer convolution. A explains only the first.

differences.what: The power of p for each of the seven dominant rows, from which the margins g_i are read.

Justifications of further rows (simultaneous rounds, axis exposure by peeling a bit, chirp numerators, packed products with the established multiplier) and the exceptional-record sorting bound O(Vp^{A'}2^{-K})=o(V).

items.note: Both carry the table of normalized costs, the margins g_1..g_7 with min g_2=eps c(1-tau)=2^-181=2kappa, setup p^{A+C}=o(Tp), log-power absorption, the final O(Tp p^{1-kappa})=O(n(log n)^{1-kappa}) and the schoolbook cutoff. A's per-row powers balance B's extra row justifications.
Neither plan states the eventual-lower-bound formulation or the liminf argument (lines 379-387); both only list the conjecture as a dependency of S0.

chain.note: Both reach the theorem by the paper's route: interchange and layer procedures, ring convolution, resampling with retained permutations, the CRT map, exact recovery and cost. On the bit side both chains are intact: s_b<W_b m, then s/W<m^tau, then F_k=O(e^tau). On the complex side A's chain thins out. It never says what the labels are. Its saving step K3/K3.C is generic and bit-only, with no s_c formula, no eta_c and no sigma. The phase-interface derivation is missing (weight additivity, translation kernels, 27-coordinate repair), and so is the P_M change of basis that turns kernels into slot calls. Yet A's layer recurrence uses a=s/W<=m^sigma (S3.3.e). B carries every link: indicator labels, then L<N/2, then s_b and s_c, then eta_b and eta_c, then tau=sigma, then both recurrences, then the cost table.

overall.reason: Neither plan contradicts the paper, so the decision rests on the core derivations. B has the essential steps of the central saving that A lacks: the triple-indicator label construction and side-wire nesting (L2), the complex phase-interface mechanism (P1, P2, P4 and s_c=W_c m-2N+2L_c), the exact deficits eta_b and eta_c with sigma for the complex network (R2, R3), and the P_M change of basis in the phase-frame recursion. A's only advantages are minor items (the full exponent list, per-row powers of p, the last-position XOR, the 2n-bit output), and B's smaller additions elsewhere offset them.
